newsitem.title: USA: U.S. securities group concerned about bank reform.
newsitem.headline: U.S. securities group concerned about bank reform.

text.p: The Securities Industry Association (SIA), trade group for U.S. investment banks and broker-dealers, said on Wednesday that although it was pleased the Treasury Department has taken a position on modernization of the financial services industry it believes the proposal does not go far enough.

In a statement, Steve Judge, SIA senior vice president for government relations, said the proposal outlined by Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin "...is clearly not as far as we need to go in a comprehensive rewrite of Glass-Steagall laws."
The depression-era Glass-Steagall Act created separate commercial banking and securities industries.

The SIA statement said the group's concerns include delineation of the role of the Federal Reserve, regulation of a holding company, creation of an operating subsidiary and the need for functional regulation of securities activities.

The statement noted that one of the options in the Rubin plan would allow the continuation of a thrift holding company. "That's an important proposal to allow securities firms to affiliate with a financial institution that offers insured deposits and,thereby, provide a full range of financial services to their customers."

The SIA statement also said that the Treasury proposals would allow, through the creation of an uninsured wholesale financial services entity, some institutional firms to have much-needed access to the federal payments system and have limited commercial banking powers."
The securities industry has long argued that if banks get involved in securities then the activity should be subject to tthe same regulation that is imposed on securities firms.
